scenes.heading: Angles in polygons
scenes.say: A stop sign has eight equal angles. How big is each one? By the end of this video you will be able to answer that for any polygon at all.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Walk around a park and you turn one full circle
scenes.science: The exterior angles of a polygon add to 360°
scenes.breaks: at a corner that points inwards you turn the other way, so the rule here is for shapes with every corner pointing out.
scenes.say: Imagine walking around the edge of a park. At every corner you turn a little. When you are back at the start, facing the same way, you have turned one full circle, three hundred and sixty degrees. Those turns are the exterior angles. This works for shapes whose corners all point outwards.
scenes.caption: At every corner you turn a little. Back at the start, you have turned one full circle: 360°. Those turns are the exterior angles.

scenes.heading: Split it into triangles
scenes.say: First a pentagon, then the diagonals from one corner. They split it into three triangles. Any shape with n sides splits into n minus two triangles, and each triangle holds one hundred and eighty degrees.
scenes.caption: Diagonals from one corner split a pentagon into three triangles. An n-sided shape splits into n − 2 triangles, each holding 180°.

scenes.heading: The angle sum
scenes.say: So the angle sum is n minus two, times one hundred and eighty. A pentagon has five hundred and forty degrees. A hexagon has seven hundred and twenty.
scenes.caption: Angle sum = (n − 2) × 180°. A pentagon: 540°. A hexagon: 720°.

scenes.heading: Interior + exterior = 180°
scenes.say: Here is a regular hexagon with one side extended. The exterior angle is three hundred and sixty divided by six, which is sixty degrees. It sits on a straight line with the interior angle, so the interior angle is one hundred and twenty.
scenes.caption: Regular hexagon: exterior angle = 360 ÷ 6 = 60°. Interior + exterior = 180°, so the interior angle is 120°.

scenes.heading: Working backwards
scenes.question: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°. How many sides?
scenes.say: Each interior angle is one hundred and fifty-six degrees. The exterior angle is one hundred and eighty minus that, twenty-four degrees. The exterior angles add to three hundred and sixty, so divide: three hundred and sixty divided by twenty-four is fifteen sides.
scenes.caption: Exterior = 180 − 156 = 24°. Exterior angles add to 360°, so n = 360 ÷ 24 = 15 sides.

scenes.say: Quick recap. The angle sum is n minus two times one hundred and eighty. In a regular polygon, divide by n. Exterior angles always add to three hundred and sixty, so the number of sides is three hundred and sixty divided by the exterior angle. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Angle sum = (n − 2) × 180°. Regular: divide by n. Exterior angles add to 360°, so n = 360 ÷ exterior angle. Now try the practice questions!
